I am an old woman, 67 years, and I have farmed this land since I was a young bride. Here in Mtwara the soil is sandy and tired, but I know it. I have no money to throw at fertilizer from the shop — my neighbors here mostly grow cassava and cashew, and those of us who plant maize do it the way our mothers did. I will put the goat and chicken droppings I have saved on the plot, use the seeds I kept from last harvest, and weed with my own hands and my grandchildren's help when they come from school.
